players.product: Data-center cooling (Airedale chillers/CRAHs, liquid cooling) — pure-play after PT spin

quarterly_data.signal: First quarter reported under the new three-segment structure (Data Centers, Commercial HVAC, Performance Technologies). Data Center segment revenue increased 90% year-over-year — Americas sales grew 112% and EMEA sales increased 18%, 'mainly from growth with strategic hyperscale and colocation customers' — but was down sequentially from Q4 because component shortages limited production volume. Data Center adjusted EBITDA grew 27%, giving a 14.8% adjusted EBITDA margin (down year-over-year). Total company sales rose 28%; adjusted EPS was $1.53, 44% higher than the prior year; adjusted EBITDA grew 5% (a $5.1 million increase) with margin down 270 basis points to 12.2% and gross margin down 340 basis points to 20.8%.
quarterly_data.figure: DC revenue +90% YoY (Americas +112%, EMEA +18%); DC adj EBITDA +27%, margin 14.8%; total sales +28%, adj EPS $1.53 (+44%)

quarterly_data.signal: Component shortages were the quarter's defining constraint. Critical suppliers 'essentially shut a lot of us down with a hard stop' and the shortages hit faster and lasted longer than anticipated; Modine had previously flagged four suppliers as potential vulnerabilities in its risk-management process. Because plants were already being staffed and prepared for significantly higher volume, the part shortages caused temporary downtime and lower-than-planned capacity utilisation across the expansion sites: excess labour plus unfavourable overhead absorption on the lower volumes had a 450-550 basis point impact on Data Center margin in the quarter, on top of a 150 basis point year-over-year warranty variance from a large prior-year settlement. Modine repositioned available parts to its highest-producing, most efficient lines and idled others, and rationed supply so that its largest key accounts got priority over smaller customers. By the third month of the quarter (June) Data Center margin was 'right back where we'd expect it to be,' and management said it has now secured the supply chain needed to meet demand for the rest of the year.
quarterly_data.figure: 450-550 bps Data Center margin impact from excess labour/overhead absorption; 150 bps warranty variance; four suppliers flagged as vulnerable; June margin back to normal

quarterly_data.signal: Structural response to the shortage: Modine is actively negotiating long-term agreements with its critical component suppliers covering FY 2028 and FY 2029 and expects them in place soon, its existing suppliers are expanding capacity to meet market demand, and in one instance Modine is considering vertical integration. Management noted it has doubled supply-chain spend year after year as the business has grown, and has brought in senior operations talent at plant level to negotiate these long-term contracts and dynamically rebalance launch schedules against available component capacity.
quarterly_data.figure: supplier LTAs targeted for FY2028 and FY2029; vertical integration under consideration in one case

quarterly_data.signal: Third consecutive quarter of record order intake, driving another significant increase in backlog (analysts on the call referred to backlog more than doubling; management did not quantify it). The drivers were the three largest data-center customers — a couple of hyperscalers plus one large neocloud provider — all raising their forecasts as their data-center build-outs grow; none were named on the call. Order growth is concentrated in air handling units and chillers. On coverage, Modine typically starts a fiscal year with roughly 70%-80% of revenue in firm orders, with firm POs about six months out (two quarters), softer visibility in Q3 and no firm POs yet in Q4 — those Q4 POs, including against the hyperscaler capacity LTA, arrive as the year rolls forward.
quarterly_data.figure: third straight record order quarter; roughly 70%-80% of fiscal-year revenue in firm orders at year start; firm POs about six months out

quarterly_data.signal: The hyperscaler chiller capacity LTA has begun converting into orders: Modine has already taken a couple of orders against it and expected more 'as early as next week,' in line with its Q4 order-intake expectation, on a typical four-to-six-month lead time from order to build. Management gave the roll-out cadence for the first time: 20%-25% of the agreement in 2027 and 35%-40% in each of 2028 and 2029. The LTA absorbs about half of Modine's chiller capacity, a share expected to fall over time as product manufacturing gets more efficient and the three-megawatt chiller launches. Other customers are in discussions for their own agreements, but sized at 12-18 months rather than the three-year scale of the first hyperscaler deal.
quarterly_data.figure: LTA cadence 20%-25% in 2027 and 35%-40% in each of 2028 and 2029; ~half of chiller capacity; follow-on agreements sized at 12-18 months

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal 2027 outlook unchanged: total company sales to grow 20%-35%, Data Center segment sales 60%-80%, Commercial HVAC 5%-10%, Performance Technologies flat to up 5%. Adjusted EBITDA of $650 million-$680 million, a growth rate in excess of 40%, implying at least 100-200 basis points of margin improvement with all three segments improving; free cash flow of 4%-6% of sales. The Data Center segment specifically is expected to generate earnings growth in excess of 85% this year. Management also reaffirmed the 50%-70% Data Center organic growth framework previously laid out for fiscal 2028 ('we're confident in the numbers that we put out'), and noted Data Center revenue has compounded at more than 80% a year over the last three years.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2027: DC sales +60%-80%, total sales +20%-35%, adj EBITDA $650-680M (+40%+); DC segment earnings growth in excess of 85%; FY2028 DC +50%-70% reaffirmed

quarterly_data.signal: Margin recovery path quantified: Data Center revenue is expected to rise about $100 million sequentially in Q2, putting it back ahead of the Q4 FY2026 level and lifting the segment's adjusted EBITDA margin back to 19%-20% from 14.8% as fixed costs are re-absorbed. Management expects a further step-up in Q3 over Q2 and again in Q4, with the second half operating above the 20% EBITDA margin range for the first time in a while. Company-wide, Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to lift roughly 200-250 basis points sequentially.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 Data Center revenue +~$100M sequentially, margin back to 19%-20%; second half above 20%; company margin +200-250 bps in Q2

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity ceiling stated: with the capex already deployed and the facilities and rooftops it has in place today, Modine believes the range is 'right around $4 billion' of revenue it can support over time. Going beyond that would require a different level of capex outlay, or a combination of an incremental facility, more efficiency on existing lines, and leveraging the supply chain to produce overflow capacity; design work is moving toward a more modular systems approach in the factory to add flexibility. The remaining chiller lines in Grenada, Jefferson City and the Dallas area are expected to be up and established at some level of efficiency by the end of the fiscal year. Coils production has been consolidated into Grenada and Juarez to allow the Grenada chiller lines to expand while preserving coil capacity for data-center customers; Heat Transfer Solutions sales improved 7%, or $11 million, on strong North America coil volume supporting data-center customers.
quarterly_data.figure: ~$4 billion of revenue capacity on current capex and footprint; Grenada, Jefferson City and Dallas chiller lines running by end of fiscal 2027; coil sales +7% / $11M on data-center demand

quarterly_data.signal: Technology read-through on evolving cooling architectures: asked whether higher inlet fluid temperature specs for future GPU designs reduce chiller demand, management said demand is improving and increasing for Modine because of its free-cooling technology — a higher inlet temperature lets the unit run in free-cooling mode more of the time, driving further efficiency and reducing data-center power consumption, while the chiller and refrigerant cycle stay in place as the 'insurance policy' for temperatures above that band. Chillers support both facility cooling and incorporation into direct-to-chip liquid cooling systems — similar models and SKUs sit on the same data-center rooftop doing both — so Modine cannot split its order book between the two. The enhanced three-megawatt chiller is being introduced to customers and will raise output per line versus the 2 MW unit.
quarterly_data.figure: 3 MW chiller launching (vs 2 MW today); higher GPU inlet temperatures increase free-cooling/chiller demand

quarterly_data.signal: A customer program delay pushed volume out of the quarter: the modular data-center product being co-designed with a specific hyperscaler is in roughly its third iteration of the design cycle, and updates to the prints and overall product specifications moved the build out of Q1. Management stressed this was a new product launch slipping, not chiller orders being cancelled or pushed out. A few shipments also slipped at the very end of the quarter. Modine's other new product launches were described as a commercial success, with the strategic customer focus on 'high-quality hyperscalers, neoclouds, and co-location customers.'

Performance Technologies spin-off and Reverse Morris Trust merger with Gentherm remains on track to close before the end of calendar 2026: Gentherm has completed its S-4 submission to the SEC, Modine has completed the filing for an IRS determination letter on the tax treatment and expects a favourable ruling before close, and IT separation plus legal-entity reorganisation are under way. Corporate SG&A carried $7.1 million of spin-related expenses in the quarter, primarily professional services. Post-spin, as a pure HVAC and Data Center company, management estimates a 7%-10% gross margin lift, with Commercial HVAC and Data Centers both able to operate at a 30% type gross margin. Fiscal 2027 guidance still includes Performance Technologies for the full year; PT will move to discontinued operations in the quarter the transaction closes.
quarterly_data.figure: $7.1M spin costs in Q1; ~7%-10% gross margin lift post-spin; DC and Commercial HVAC capable of ~30% gross margin
